title: Sisi Joins Trump-Arab Leaders Multilateral Call Urging 'Diplomatic Window' to Secure Iran Nuclear Deal
detail: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi participated in a multilateral phone call with US President Donald Trump, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed, Turkish President Erdogan, Jordan's King Abdullah II, Bahrain's King Hamad, Qatar's Amir Tamim, and Pakistan's Army Chief. Sisi urged the group to capitalize on what he described as a 'diplomatic window' to achieve a comprehensive, binding agreement on Iran's nuclear program. Egypt proposed a potential US-Iran 'memorandum of understanding' framework as a potential structuring mechanism for any deal. The call represents the highest-level multilateral engagement on the Iran nuclear track since resumption of US-Iran talks, and marks Egypt's consolidation of a central regional diplomatic role — reflecting a significant evolution from Mubarak-era passivity toward active regional mediation under Sisi.

media.caption: Sisi urges diplomatic window to secure US-Iran deal in multilateral call with Trump and Arab leaders

title: Egypt Intensifies Iran Mediation; Abdelatty Contacts Iranian FM Araghchi and Qatari Premier
detail: Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held separate phone calls with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani as part of an intensive week of regional diplomacy around the US-Iran nuclear negotiations. Abdelatty also met in Cairo with Algeria's FM Ahmed Attaf and Tunisia's FM Mohamed Ali Nafti, building North African and Arab consensus around the terms of a potential US-Iran agreement. Egypt has emerged throughout the negotiation period as a bridge between Western demands and Middle Eastern and Iranian regional concerns — a role that reflects the evolution of Cairo's post-2024 foreign policy from reactive mediation to proactive regional architecture-building.

media.caption: Cairo contacts Tehran over US-Iran talks as Egypt intensifies its regional diplomatic role
